title: tshark: Support --read-file and filter long opts
description:
The tshark man page and help claims to support the --read-file,
--read-filter, and --display-filter long options. Make it so.

Programs have to dissect in order to run filters, so add the filtering
options to dissect_opts.h, which Wireshark, tshark, and rawshark
already include, so that they stay consistent between applications.

Reading a file is a common activity that we might want to have
more (all?) command line tools support with the same syntax
eventually, so add that to clopts_common.h

rawshark doesn't distinguish between read filters and display
filters; to make things easy and consistent, make them synonymous
for rawshark.

Fix #19365

notes.body: Should we add or modify existing tests as well?
Sure, I'll add a small test for the long opts.

added 3 commits
  • 7d17a5fb...50f322ec - 2 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • e4d6eb94 - tshark: Support --read-file and filter long opts
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/12569/diffs?diff_id=814736039&start_sha=7d17a5fb300df7bf851bc81f2677198f87acf7cd)

> Programs have to dissect in order to run filters, so add these options to dissect_opts.h

But `-r`/`--read-file` doesn't have anything to do with dissecting; it's mainly there for TShark, to tell it to read a capture file rather than capturing on the default interface (in imitation of tcpdump), so perhaps it should be in a separate `#define`.

The filter long options connection with dissection is also a bit indirect.

I might be inclined to remove `DISSECT_` from `LONGOPT_DISSECT_READ_CAPTURE_COMMON` and `OPTSTRING_DISSECT_READ_CAPTURE_COMMON`, and put them in a different header.
Sure. I considered putting them in a separate new header file that would have only the defines, that is reasonable.

> The filter long options connection with dissection is also a bit indirect.

It's a bit indirect, but in order to use a display/read filter (as opposed to a capture filter), a program has to be able to dissect.

It's true that there are a number of programs that read files, and we might want them all to support the same option.

So another option I might be inclined to is adding the filtering options to the `LONGOPT_DISSECT_COMMON` (even though they are handled in the individual programs themselves), and having `-r/--read-file` in a separate `#define`.

--R  <read (display) filter>::

+rather than that of capture filters) to be applied before printing the output.
+Read filters and display filters are synonymous in *rawshark*.
+--
+
 include::dissection-options.adoc[tags=!tshark;!decode_as]

@@ -79,6 +79,12 @@ class TestBasicClopts:
         process = subprocesstest.run((cmd_tshark, '-r', capture_file('dhcp.pcap')), env=test_env)
         assert process.returncode == ExitCodes.OK
 
+    def test_existing_file_longopt(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        # $TSHARK -r "${CAPTURE_DIR}dhcp.pcap" > ./testout.txt 2>&1
+        process = subprocesstest.run((cmd_tshark, '--read-file', capture_file('dhcp.pcap'),

     def test_nonexistent_file(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
